---
title: "Models vs Platforms/Providers"
---

## Models vs Developers vs Providers

::: {.incremental}
- **Model** — the trained neural network itself (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Llama 3.3 70B)
- **Developer** — the lab that trains and releases the model (OpenAI → GPT-4.1, Anthropic → Claude, Meta → Llama, Alibaba → Qwen)
- **Provider / platform** — hosts and serves models via API (OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub Models, Groq, Azure)
- Developer ≈ provider as well for proprietary models (OpenAI both trains *and* serves GPT-4.1)
    - But also... GitHub/Azure serve GPT as well (with their limitations) and many other models
- Developer ≠ provider for open models (Meta trains Llama → Groq, AWS, Azure *serve* it)
:::

. . .

In `chatlas`, switching providers means changing one constructor:

```python
from chatlas import ChatOpenAI, ChatAnthropic, ChatGithub, ChatGroq

chat = ChatGithub(model="gpt-4.1-mini")      # free, 8k input cap by default
chat = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4.1-mini")      # paid, full 1M context
chat = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-sonnet-4-6-20250514")  # paid, 200k (1M beta)
chat = ChatGroq(model="llama-3.3-70b-versatile")          # free, 128k context
```

::: {.notes}
Key point: the model is the same GPT-4.1-mini whether you access it through GitHub Models or OpenAI directly. What changes is the limits and pricing the provider imposes. The `Chat*` constructor names refer to the **provider**, not the developer. For Anthropic and OpenAI these happen to be the same company; for GitHub Models they're different.
:::


## Context Window vs Provider Input Limit

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

**Context window** = total token budget for one API call (input + output).

- **GPT-4.1 family**: 1M context, 32k max output
- **Claude 4.6 (Sonnet/Opus)**: 200k standard, 1M beta
- **Llama 3.3 70B**: 128k context

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

**But providers can cap it lower:**

- GitHub Models playground limits GPT-4.1-mini to **8k input by default** — that's 0.8% of the model's 1M capacity!
- Same model, same weights, vastly different limits

:::
:::

. . .

Effective max input ≈ context window − max output tokens.
A "1M context" model with 32k max output → ~968k usable input.


## Provider Limitations (Not Model Limitations) {.smaller}

| Provider | Models | Model Context | Provider Input Limit | Rate Limit | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub Models| gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4.1 | 1M | **8k tokens** | 150 req/day (mini) | Free |
| OpenAI (direct) | gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4.1 | 1M | 1M | Pay-per-use | $0.40/$1.60 (mini) |
| Anthropic | Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6 | 200k (1M beta) | 200k (1M beta) | Pay-per-use | $3/$15 (Sonnet) |
| Groq (free) | Llama 3.3, Qwen3, gpt-oss | 128k | 128k | 30 req/min | Free tier |
| Groq (paid) | same + more | 128k | 128k | Higher limits | $0.05–$1.00 |
| Azure OpenAI | gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4.1 | 1M | up to 1M | Configurable | ≈ OpenAI |

GitHub Models is a playground: the 8k input cap is a huge difference from the model's 1M context.
We will hit this limit when sending PDFs or long conversations.
The 150 req/day cap also means querychat can burn through the budget in a single session.



## Pricing Deep Dive

Output tokens cost 2-5x more than input tokens. Why? Reading is cheap (and sometimes parallelizable); *generating* is expensive.

| Model | Developer | Provider | Context | Input $/1M | Output $/1M | Free? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-4.1-mini | OpenAI | OpenAI | 1M | $0.40 | $1.60 | ❌ |
| gpt-4.1-mini | OpenAI | GitHub Models | 1M (8k cap) | — | — | ✅ |
| gpt-4.1 | OpenAI | OpenAI | 1M | $2.00 | $8.00 | ❌ |
| Sonnet 4.6 | Anthropic | Anthropic | 200k (1M beta) | $3.00 | $15.00 | ❌ |
| Opus 4.6 | Anthropic | Anthropic | 200k (1M beta) | $5.00 | $25.00 | ❌ |
| Llama 3.3 70B | Meta | Groq | 128k | $0.59 | $0.79 | free tier |
| Qwen3 32B | Alibaba | Groq | 131k | $0.29 | $0.59 | free tier |

. . .

**Real example:** extracting data from a PDF with Anthropic Sonnet:
23k input tokens, 1.5k output tokens = **$0.09**
More importantly, some other models won't deal with multimodal (binary files) input.
. . .


## iClicker: Model, Developer, or Provider?

```python
from querychat import QueryChat
from chatlas import ChatAnthropic

qc = QueryChat(df, "tips",
    client=ChatAnthropic(model="claude-sonnet-4-6-20250514"))
```

In this code, `ChatAnthropic(...)` tells chatlas which **\_\_\_\_** to connect to.

A. Model
B. Developer
C. Provider / platform
D. Dataset
E. System prompt
